metadata.note: Representative markers for New England bike-share and e-bike-share systems that publish no public GBFS feed (or whose feed is key-gated). One marker per member municipality, or per home station where the operator publishes exact locations (CargoB). Markers are not live station status. Systems with public GBFS feeds (Bluebikes, Veo Hartford, Veo New Haven, Spin Providence) are drawn live by the shared-mobility layer instead.
metadata.geocoding: Town-center markers geocoded with Nominatim (OpenStreetMap, ODbL); CargoB hubs from the operator’s public station map.

properties.title: ValleyBike Share · Springfield
properties.details: Pedal-assist e-bike share jointly owned by nine Pioneer Valley municipalities and UMass Amherst, operated by Drop Mobility since the August 2024 relaunch. Rentals through the ValleyBike app. Drop Mobility’s GBFS feed is key-gated, so live dock counts are not shown. Marker sits at the town center, not at a dock; the operator app shows exact stations and availability.

properties.title: Rideable Nashua
properties.details: Community bike share designed and run by Drop Mobility for the City of Nashua: 50 e-bikes at more than 10 stations, $1.50 to unlock plus $0.25 per minute in the Drop app, with hardship discounts. Drop Mobility’s GBFS feed is key-gated, so live dock counts are not shown. Marker sits at the town center, not at a dock; the operator app shows exact stations and availability.

properties.title: Portland Bike Share
properties.status: Public bike share · 200 bikes at 40+ stations
properties.details: City of Portland and Tandem Mobility system on the Portland peninsula: classic and e-assist bikes, $1 to unlock plus $0.30 per minute, $14.99 monthly or $99 annual membership, rentals through the Movatic app. No public GBFS feed is published, so live dock counts are not shown. Marker sits at the town center, not at a dock; the operator app shows exact stations and availability.

properties.title: Port Bikeshare · Newburyport
properties.status: Public bike share · 5 stations on the Clipper City Rail Trail
properties.details: 23 pedal bikes and 2 adaptive recumbent trikes at five stations along the Clipper City Rail Trail (Market Landing area, American Yacht Club, Custom House Way, Washington Street, March’s Hill, and Parker Street by the MBTA station). Launched November 2025 by the City, Tandem Mobility and Newburyport Livable Streets; $3 to unlock for 30 minutes, then $0.10 per minute, via the Movatic app. Marker sits at the town center, not at a dock; the operator app shows exact stations and availability.
properties.provider: City of Newburyport · Tandem Mobility · Newburyport Livable Streets

properties.title: Minuteman Bikeshare · Acton
properties.details: Regional bike share with 35 bikes at seven locations across Concord, Acton, Lincoln and Maynard, run by Tandem Mobility through the Movatic app ($2 per 30 minutes; $30 annual membership). Funded by a MassDOT Shared Streets and Spaces grant from spring 2025 through fall 2027. Marker sits at the town center, not at a dock; the operator app shows exact stations and availability.

properties.title: Metro Mobility · Boston
properties.details: Cambridge-based Metro Mobility rents e-bikes by the day from self-charging ChargeLock stations, normally returned to the same station, and runs private fleets for housing developments and employers. Public rental locations listed in its app include Boston, Somerville, Newton, Medford, Quincy, Lowell, Lawrence, Newburyport and Worcester. Marker sits at the city center; the app shows exact stations.
